# The QA matrix

<!-- GENERATED by internal/qamatrix from internal/qamatrix/registry.json.
     Regenerate with: QAMATRIX_WRITE_DOCS=1 go test ./internal/qamatrix/...
     Edit the registry, not this file. -->

The QA matrix: which of the fourteen questions has been asked of which package,
and by which named test that can be found in the tree.

A category is either a named test that EXISTS in the package's own test files,
or a reason saying why the category does not apply. A blank is a finding for a
Tier A package and a counted gap for a Tier B or C package.

This file is the source of truth. `docs/qa-matrix.md` is GENERATED from it and
the gate fails when the two disagree.

The Go tree is what this matrix covers. The console's own surface -- the React
SPA under `web/spa` -- is covered by its Vitest suite and by the `spa-coverage`
and `spa-e2e` gates, and it appears in the critical path below as a browser
spec rather than as a package.

## The fourteen categories

The set is closed. A category outside it is a question nobody agreed to ask, and a matrix whose categories are chosen per package is a matrix that only says the package is fine.

- `functional`
- `boundary`
- `error-refusal`
- `invariant`
- `state-machine`
- `concurrency`
- `durability`
- `tenant-isolation`
- `contract`
- `time`
- `security`
- `observability`
- `a11y`
- `performance`

## The critical path

Ten stages, closed. The chain is the one `AGENTS.md` protects and the one the plan names: ingest, normalize, rule match, incident, attention queue, operator read, disposition, audit ledger, checkpoint, replay.

A stage that is dropped is a stage nobody is proving, and the omission is invisible: the rest of the chain still passes. So the list lives in the code, and the registry is checked against it.

| Stage | Proved by |
|---|---|
| ingest | internal/inbox.TestAFreshWriteCarriesTheEventIdentity<br>internal/inbox.TestADeadLetterReachedThroughRetryCarriesACompletionInstant |
| normalize | internal/normalize.TestNormalizedTimeIsAlwaysUTC<br>internal/normalize.TestNormalizedTimeSubtractsTheDrift<br>internal/normalize.TestAMissingObservedTimeFallsBackToIngestAndSaysSo |
| rule-match | internal/rules.TestEvaluationIsDeterministic<br>internal/rules.TestAMatchedRuleCarriesItsDispatch<br>internal/rules.TestDegradedObservationIsNotEvidence |
| incident | internal/incidents.TestCreateIncidentStoresItsJustification<br>internal/incidents.TestAnIncidentAlwaysLinksAtLeastItsTrigger |
| attention-queue | internal/api.TestTheAttentionQueueIsOrderedByTheProductsJudgement<br>internal/incidents.TestTheAttentionQueueIsOrderedAndDecays |
| operator-reads | internal/api.TestTheIncidentPageRendersTheIncident<br>internal/api.TestConsoleIncidentPageRendersProvenance<br>web/spa/e2e/console.spec.ts |
| disposition | internal/api.TestASensitiveDispositionWithoutASecondFactorIsRefused<br>internal/incidents.TestSensitiveDispositionsRequireStepUp |
| audit-ledger | internal/audit.TestConcurrentAppendsProduceOneChain<br>internal/audit.TestVerifyingASubRangeStillFindsATamperedRow |
| checkpoint | internal/checkpoint.TestVerifyAgainstSeals<br>internal/checkpoint.TestVerifyDetectsFieldTampering |
| replay | internal/incidents.TestReplayReproducesTheDecisionFromStoredFacts<br>internal/incidents.TestReplayedFromStoredFactsIsAlwaysOnTheWire |

## The blanks

740 of 1652 category slots are blank.

A blank is a category with no named test and no reason, and it is a finding for a Tier A package. For a Tier B or C package it is allowed, because the tier says how much coverage that package owes -- but it is printed here and counted, because a gap that is invisible is a gap that is never closed.

Covered by a named test: 527. Not applicable, with a reason: 385. Blank: 740.

A category with a named test is a category with ONE test. It is not a proof that the category is covered, and this document does not claim it is. The `red-check` table is what proves the answers bite; this matrix is what proves the answers are findable.
